label: live

steps.assertion: The Pro project terminal opens in its registered dedicated checkout.
The dev-madrid device terminal uses the existing relay and prints the actual remote hostname.
Type or dictate a command and Run send echo hello through the real PTY.
Sticky Ctrl and C interrupt sleep within two seconds and preserve its non-zero exit record.
Reload reconnects the same terminal and replays hello in its scrollback.
The copy buttons include exactly the requested command range and strip every escape code.

steps.assertion: Send to… delivers the last command to the coordinator and starts its next turn.

steps.assertion: Take over in browser attaches a real native thread session; leaving detaches and returns it to Jevellan.
Every captured screen passes the dedicated live vision rubric in this layout.

screens.expected: a connected project terminal with usable controls and no clipped text

cosmetic: The host and path in the header are cut short with an ellipsis ('/Users/ggomes…'), so the full project path isn't visible.
The rightmost button in the special-key row is partly cut off at the right edge. The row probably scrolls sideways, but nothing shows that more keys are there.
The terminal output wraps mid-word ('jevellan-l / ive-sandbox'), which is a little harder to read.
The terminal area has a lot of empty space while the special-key row runs out of width.

screens.expected: a connected dev-madrid terminal with the remote hostname and usable controls

cosmetic: The row of special keys is cut off at the right edge: a partly visible button after '→' suggests the row scrolls sideways, but nothing on screen says so.
There are two header bars, each with its own menu button ('Conversations' and 'Terminal'), which repeats the navigation and wastes vertical space.
A stray 'hostname' line appears above the first prompt, apparently an echo of the command before the shell prompt drew.
The terminal output area is mostly empty and a faint horizontal line runs near its bottom edge.

screens.expected: terminal copy and Send to controls reachable at this layout

cosmetic: The key-bar row is clipped at both edges: the leftmost button (→) is cut off on the left and the … button sits right against the right edge. It looks like a horizontal scroller with no visible scroll cue.
The header path is cut off with an ellipsis (/Users/ggomes...).
The long shell prompt wraps onto two lines, which makes the terminal output harder to scan.
The 'Copied' status label floats on its own above the input field, a long way from the button that triggered it.

screens.expected: a browser terminal attached to a resumed native coding session, past setup and trust dialogs, with usable exit controls

cosmetic: The row of keys (Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, arrows) is cut off on the right: the last key is only partly visible at the screen edge. The row probably scrolls sideways.
The terminal footer line 'bypass permissions on (shift+tab to' is cut off at the right edge.
The header subtitle 'dev-madrid scenarios · /home/ggo...' is shortened with an ellipsis.
The terminal shows a non-blocking stop hook error ('/Users/ggomes/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin/node: not found'). This is a problem in the session's setup, not in the screen layout.

observations: Usage records come from runtime-reported turn outcomes. Missing tokens or cost remain unknown; minutes include concurrent sessions.
